Socialism, or at least hardcore socialism as opposed to 'democratic socialism', is premised around the point that in general society the people that actually run things see very little in the way of fruits of their labor. If a business has 100 workers and one person who owns the machines being used to make the product, it's pretty typical that something like 99% of the generated wealth gets redistributed away from the people creating it and into the hands of the person who owns the machines. Socialism, and this is hardcore socialism no less, isn't about getting rid of capitalism but instead improving the lives of more people in a capitalist system.

'Democratic socialism', as endorsed by folks like Sanders, is an even more softball version of this where we continue to let the 0.1% take nearly all the wealth but then take a cut of that to provide basic necessities - education, healthcare, etc - for the rest of society.
